annotations.grafana.app/message: Manage SOMA storage observability dashboard as code

spec.description: Production health, traffic, latency, retries, safe failure logs, and traces for Soma's Supabase Storage boundaries.
Failed provider attempts as a share of all observed provider attempts over 5 minutes. Retries count again; this is not a unique-session or business-failure rate.
spec.title: Provider attempt error ratio

spec.description: Failed storage provider attempts per minute. Repeated retries of one object are counted separately.
spec.title: Failed provider calls / min

spec.description: Storage retry events per minute. Compare with failed calls to see retry amplification.
spec.title: Retries / min

spec.description: P95 duration of provider attempts. Fast failures can lower this value, so it is not a success-latency SLI.
spec.title: P95 provider-call latency

spec.description: Successful provider attempts as a share of all attempts over five minutes. Retries count as additional attempts; this does not prove unique workflows completed.
spec.title: Successful provider attempts

spec.description: Failed provider attempts as a share of all attempts over five minutes. Repeated retries of one object are counted separately.
spec.title: Failed provider attempts

options.content:
**These are provider-attempt diagnostics, not business outcomes.** A retry is another provider attempt, so a single session can produce many failures. Use the failure logs and traces to identify the upstream response, then use workflow-level telemetry to decide customer impact.

`soma_storage_transfer_bytes_total` records bytes attempted by the application. Bytes on an error series were not confirmed stored. Missing telemetry renders as **Unknown**, never as a healthy zero.

spec.description: Provider attempts per second split by workflow, operation, and outcome.
spec.title: Storage provider attempt rate

spec.description: Failed provider attempts as a percentage of attempts, split by workflow. Retries count again and can dominate this ratio.
spec.title: Provider attempt error ratio by workflow

spec.description: P95 provider-attempt latency by workflow and operation. Failure and success attempts are combined.
spec.title: P95 latency by operation

spec.description: Application payload bytes supplied to provider calls per second. Error series are attempted bytes, not confirmed storage.
spec.title: Attempted payload throughput

spec.description: Payload-blind provider failures with safe upstream diagnostics. Expand a line and follow its trace ID when one is present.
spec.title: Storage failure logs

spec.query: { name =~ "storage\\..+" && span.storage.provider = "supabase" && span.storage.workflow =~ "$workflow" && span.storage.logical_area =~ "$logical_area" && status = error }

spec.description: Failed storage client spans. Open a row to inspect the complete request trace and surrounding workflow.
spec.title: Failed storage traces

spec.expr: sum by (upstream_status, service_name) (count_over_time({service_name=~"soma-.+"} | json | event="storage_operation_failed" | workflow=~"$workflow" | logical_area=~"$logical_area" [5m]))

spec.description: Failure events in each rolling five-minute window by upstream status and runtime. A missing series means no matching failure logs.
spec.title: 5m failures by upstream status and service

spec.description: Retry, fallback, and conflict events emitted by the storage boundary.
spec.title: Retries, fallbacks and conflicts

spec.description: 1 while the session-archive circuit breaker is open and uploads are being shed. While open, upload attempts never reach the provider, so the failure panels go quiet for a reason that is not recovery.
spec.title: Archive breaker

spec.description: Upload attempts refused inside the process per minute. These produce no provider call and therefore no success or error sample.
spec.title: Uploads shed / min

spec.description: Upload attempts admitted to the provider per minute. Compare with the error rate: a falling error rate with a falling allow rate is shedding, not recovery.
spec.title: Uploads allowed / min

spec.description: Snapshots whose content and completion flags matched the last stored copy, so no upload was needed.
spec.title: Duplicates skipped / min

spec.description: Every upload decision, including the ones that never leave the process. This is the only place a shed attempt is visible; storage_operations counts provider calls only.
spec.title: Admission decisions

spec.description: Periods when uploads were shed process-wide. Read the failure panels against this: quiet failures inside an open window mean nothing was attempted.
spec.title: Breaker open periods

spec.description: Successful reads from the transcript source. This is the baseline the refusal count is meaningless without: zero refusals with zero reads is a stopped system, not a healthy one.
spec.title: Transcript reads OK / min

spec.description: Reads the pacer gave up on. terminal is a 401 or 403 from the source; exhausted is a run of failures. A refused read issues no HTTP request, so outbound volume falls when this rises.
spec.title: Transcript reads refused / min

spec.description: Transcripts that actually reached storage. Distinct from the allowed rate above: an admitted upload can still fail at the provider.
spec.title: Uploads completed / min

spec.description: Every admission decision, allowed or refused. If this reaches zero no archival is being attempted at all, which every other panel on this tab renders as calm.
spec.title: Decisions / min

spec.description: Reads against the transcript source by result. failed backs off and retries; terminal and exhausted stop that session's polling entirely. The MacBook sits behind the same edge as storage, so a block here is reachable too.
spec.title: Transcript read outcomes

spec.description: P95 delay the pacer chose. Sitting at the configured interval means healthy polling; climbing means reads are failing and backing off.
spec.title: Backoff before the next read

spec.expr: sum by (upstream_body_marker, upstream_status) (count_over_time({service_name=~"soma-.+"} | json | event="storage_operation_failed" | upstream_body_marker != "" [5m]))

spec.description: The edge's own reason code parsed from non-JSON error bodies. cloudflare_1015 is rate limiting, which expires on a timer; cloudflare_1020 is a firewall rule, which does not. A missing series means no edge block pages were returned.
spec.title: Edge block reason codes
